docs.title: Statistical astrophysics at scale
docs.text: I use rigorous statistical techniques to solve novel problems in astrophysics, with a focus on fast radio bursts (FRBs) through the CHIME/FRB Collaboration. My work connects population inference to the physical questions hidden in large transient datasets.

docs.title: About me
docs.text:
I am a PhD student in Physics at McGill University, co-supervised by Vicky Kaspi and Jason Hessels, and a member of the CHIME/FRB Collaboration. My research develops statistically rigorous ways to study fast radio bursts and the populations revealed by real-time radio surveys.

I am especially interested in the interface between survey design, observational selection effects, and population-level inference. These tools help turn rapidly growing FRB samples into reliable constraints on their sources and environments.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Research projects in transient astrophysics, survey science, and statistical inference.

01 · Survey selection

Selection functions connect the underlying population to detected events.

02 · FRB populations

Unifying repeating and apparent non-repeating FRBs

Some FRB sources repeat while many have been observed only once. This project tests whether those groups can arise from a shared underlying population after accounting for observing cadence, source activity, and the probability of detecting another burst.

Question When does a source appear to be a one-off because of its physics, and when because of how it was observed?

Forecasting how repeater detections grow with survey time and sensitivity.

03 · Early-Universe constraints

Forecasting cosmic-string limits with radio transient surveys

Radio transient surveys can test models of the early Universe. I develop forecasts for how next-generation facilities may constrain cosmic-string populations through their predicted transient signatures.

Approach Translate survey design and null results into robust upper limits on cosmic-string models.

Illustration of density wakes from smooth and perturbed cosmic strings.

docs.title: Measuring observational bias in real-time FRB surveys
docs.text:
Triggered surveys do not observe every burst equally. I model how detection thresholds, real-time triggering, and instrumental sensitivity transform an intrinsic FRB population into an observed sample.

Goal Build population analyses that carry survey selection effects through to the final inference.

docs.title: Research & Publications
docs.text:
I study fast radio burst populations with methods designed for the realities of modern, real-time astronomical surveys.

Within the CHIME/FRB Collaboration, I use population models, simulations, and Bayesian inference to study the sources and environments of fast radio bursts. By accounting for how survey selection effects shape the bursts we detect, I connect CHIME/FRB's growing sample to the underlying astrophysical population.
